scope: Every ratio compares the medians of three samples per mode from one matched runner and one immutable 0ffa AOT package. No timings, distributions or ratios are pooled across jobs or source snapshots.

The original legacy control does not register the custom canvas island; the explicit legacy-composite mode combines cached original document and feedback pixels using Uno's original uploader. Both modes use the same current application bytes.
These two experiments do not compare against the original 96e baseline and cannot establish baseline recovery or default promotion. The candidate default remains outside this opt-in comparison.

Six primary samples determine each comparison. Two managed-diagnostic runs are separate and excluded from all primary medians and ratios. Actual initialization, cache reuse and layer isolation remain mode-specific contracts.
These 18 native before/after/restored pairs cover the Welcome timing fixture at DPR 1. Broader Welcome lifecycle, fractional-DPR and extended-SVG quality are separate gates.
ThreadTime measures active renderer main-thread CPU and excludes GPU and worker CPU. TaskDuration is elapsed task time and may include waits; neither is native GPU execution time.

Offered operations per second, completed callbacks and visible-canvas submissions are not physical frames or proven input-to-new-pixels latency. Every trusted input passes the original later-callback and graphics observations, which do not prove a newer scene recording.
All primary windows exclude startup, common warmup, screenshots and restore validation. Total experiment duration includes those phases and the separate diagnostics.

Upload counts and supplied JavaScript buffer bytes are API observations, not measured physical transfer bytes. Full raw browser observations, console logs and native PNGs remain bound to the source report and immutable artifact digests.
